desc:
WooCommerce plugin onboarding and conversion work helps more installs turn into stores that finish setup and, where relevant, upgrade. Ecom Swift LLC walks through your plugin as a new owner would, then improves notices, setup flow, wording and upgrade screens.

## What is WooCommerce plugin onboarding?

It is everything a store owner sees from the moment they activate your plugin until they use its main feature for the first time. That includes the first screen, the setup steps, the settings labels, the notices and the upgrade page.

Conversion in this context has two stages. The first is turning an install into an active store that has completed setup. The second is turning a satisfied free user into a paying one, for plugins that offer a Pro version.

## Why do many installs never become active stores?

A store owner installs a plugin with a goal in mind, usually in a hurry. If the first screen is a blank settings page with twenty options, they close it. If a required step is hidden in a submenu, the plugin never starts working, and they conclude it does not work.

Those users rarely complain. They quietly deactivate, and you never learn why. Looking at the plugin through a new owner's eyes shows these gaps quickly.

## How clearer onboarding affects installs and upgrades

People upgrade when they have already seen value. A user who finished setup and saw the plugin work is far more open to a paid feature than one who never got started. So the order matters: first get the free experience right, then show the upgrade at a natural moment.

Respectful prompts also protect your reputation. A notice that cannot be dismissed, or that appears on every admin page, trains people to distrust the plugin. A short, dismissible notice tied to a feature the user just tried feels like help instead of pressure.

## What a good onboarding and upgrade experience includes

- A clear first screen after activation that says what to do next.
- A setup checklist or wizard with a small number of steps.
- Settings labels written in plain language, with short help text.
- Dismissible notices that appear once and only where relevant.
- An upgrade page that compares free and Pro features honestly.
- Consent-based usage tracking that asks before collecting anything.
- A short feedback question when someone deactivates.
- A welcome email that points to the first useful action.
- Test setups, so changes can be measured instead of guessed.

## What we do

We install the plugin on a fresh WordPress and WooCommerce site and behave like a first-time owner. We record each place we hesitate, misread a label or cannot find the next step. These notes become written findings.

Then we fix what matters most: wording, notices, the first-run screen and the order of steps. Standard and Premium packages go further, with a setup checklist or wizard, a rebuilt upgrade page, consent-based tracking and a feedback form. Premium also sets up an A/B test and writes a welcome email. We follow WordPress.org rules on notices and upsells, and we cannot promise a specific number of upgrades, because results depend on your product, price and audience.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Make the first useful action obvious within seconds of activation.
- Ask for consent before any usage tracking starts.
- Let users dismiss every notice for good.
- Describe Pro features in terms of tasks they complete.
- Review feedback from deactivations on a regular schedule.

**Avoid:**
- Showing upgrade banners on unrelated admin pages.
- Locking a core free feature behind a hidden paywall.
- Using countdown timers or pressure wording.
- Collecting data without telling users what and why.
- Changing many things at once, which makes results hard to read.

## Who this service is for

This service suits an author of a free plugin with many installs but few active stores. It suits a team with a Pro version whose upgrade page does not explain the difference. It also suits a paid plugin sold outside the directory that wants a smoother first-run experience.

## What we need from you

Send the plugin zip, a link to your listing or site and a short note on your ideal user. Tell us what you consider a successful setup. We never ask for passwords, and any access to your staging site is given as a developer or collaborator user. We will reply with a checklist after your order.
